sentences.text: Shri Pankaj Kumar Jain, learned counsel for the respond  ORDER 1.
With the consent of the learned counsel for the parties, the appeal is finally heard.

2. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant / claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 26/9/2022 passed in MACC No.211/2019 by the Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Barwani whereby a total sum of Rs.3,34,936/-
has been awarded to the appellant / claimant by way of compensation.
The appellant has challenged the quantum of compensation on several counts.
3. Short facts of the case are that on 13/3/2017, appellant was going with his friend Sumeet on motorcycle bearing registration No.M.P. 46 M.F. / 2339 to village Danod.

At around 1.30 in the night when they were near Narawala Phata, Grid, the respondent No.2/driver of offending Maruti car bearing registration No. M.P. 09 BA 8359 owned by respondent No.1 and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25069 2 MA-5820-2022 insured with respondent No.3 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed into the motorcycle of the appellant because of which he sustained grievous injuries.

He remained hospitalized for a period from 13/3/2017 to 14/3/2017 in District Hospital, Barwani and thereafter from 14/3/2017 to 16/3/2017 at Sai Baba Hospital, Barwani where he was operated upon and implant of screw and rod was inserted into his right leg.
Thereafter because of infection in the implant he had to got it remove at Apple Hospital, Indore where he remained admitted from 3/4/2018 to 7/4/2018.
4. The appellant, as such, filed claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V. Act claiming compensation for the aforesaid injuries.

The claims tribunal after concluding the rash and negligent driving of the insured vehicle awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.3,34,936/- which was Duryodhan vs Abdula on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119257400/
1 rounded off to Rs.3,35,000/-.

sentences.text: Out of this amount, an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- was for treatment and amount of Rs.50,000/- was for pain and suffering due to injuries including loss of amenities.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that claims tribunal erred in not considering that the appellant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 11.66% which was duly certified by doctor vide certificate Exhibit P/91.
He submits that in support of his permanent disability Dr. Sunil Tanwar (PW.2) came for examination before the claims tribunal.

He in unequivocal term certified the permanent disability of the appellant to the extent of 11.66% which the claims tribunal considered at 6% over all loss of earning capacity without there being any reason for the same.

Apart from this it has also been stated by the learned counsel for the appellant that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25069 3 MA-5820-2022 claims tribunal believed the claim of the appellant that he was working as mason at the time of accident still he was treated as unskilled labour whereas he should have been considered skilled labourer and accordingly the compensation should have been awarded.
He thus prays for enhancement of compensation.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Co., submits that the claims tribunal has not believed the evidence of the appellant as reflected from last part of para no.28 of the impugned award.
He also points out that although the appellant has tried to demonstrate long period of treatment.
However there is no evidence on record for proving the same.

He also submits that the claim that the appellant was working as mason at the time of accident was not established by the appellant and the claims tribunal has not recorded any conclusion with respect to the same.
He thus prays for dismissal of the appeal being bereft of merit and looking to the fact that just and proper compensation of Rs.3,34,936/- has been awarded to the appellant / claimant.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8.
The appellant was a young man of 22 years on the date of his accident.
It is undisputable that he sustained permanent disability in the accident occurred on 13/3/2017.
It is also undisputed that the appellant suffered permanent disability to the extent of 11.66% into his right lower limb which has duly been certified by the doctor and believed by the tribunal.
The only question is to what extent this has resulted in loss of earning capacity of the appellant.

The appellant before the claims tribunal NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25069 4 MA-5820-2022 asserted that before accident he was doing the work of construction of house as well as poultry and cattle farming.
The claims tribunal considering his job has observed in para 32 that he can continue the same but there may be some loss of capacity which was taken at 6%.

Considering the fact that the doctor certified permanent disability in right lower limb at 11.66%, the over all loss of earning at 6% does not appear to be disproportionate hence the conclusion of the claims tribunal in this regard is not required to be interfered with.

However, on consideration of over all circumstances of the case particularly the fact that the appellant suffered permanent disability and remained hospitalized for different periods and even suffered removal of implantation due to infection, the amount of Rs.50,000/- for sustaining injuries which includes the amount of loss of amenities also appears to be very less.
Thus in the considered view of this Court, if a lumpsum amount of Rs.75,000/- is awarded then it will constitute a just compensation.
Hence the appellant is directed to be paid an amount of Rs.75,000/- over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.

This additional amount of Rs.75,000/-

2 shall carry the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of application before the claims tribunal.
9. With the aforesaid, the appeal stands disposed off.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
